channel.title: MIND / MATTER Daily Briefing
channel.description: New research across consciousness, quantum foundations, and neuroscience.

item.title: Quantum tomography of fermion pairs in e + e − collisions: Longitudinal beam polarization effects
item.description: We present a quantum tomography study of fermion pair production at future $e^+e^-$ colliders, emphasizing how longitudinal beam polarization controls the two-qubit spin density matrix. We study the processes $e^+ e^- \to t\bar{t},\ e^+e^-\to μ^+μ^-$ and Bhabha scattering $e^+e^-\to e^+e^-$, representing the mass threshold behavior, the $Z$ pole resonance and the $s/t$-channel interplay.

item.title: Does Total Knowledge Mute Emotion? A Thought Experiment using Large Language Models
item.description: Abstract This paper examines whether comprehensive knowledge acquisition attenuates emotional experience through a thought experiment that uses large language models (LLMs). We propose that LLMs, which possess extensive propositional knowledge yet lack phenomenal consciousness, serve as philosophical instruments for isolating the knowledge variable from other cognitive attributes.

item.title: Effects of auditory sensory stimulation on consciousness and physiological parameters among individuals with disorders of consciousness: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: Objective To systematically evaluate the effects of auditory sensory stimulation (SS) on consciousness levels and physiological parameters in patients with disorders of consciousness (DOC). Furthermore, this study aimed to explore intervention characteristics based on the frequency, intensity, time, and type (FITT) framework that may influence treatment effects and to investigate potential sources of between-study heterogeneity.

item.title: Ontology-constrained multi-LLM scoring of hypothesis support in the predictive processing literature
item.description: Fragmentation is common in interdisciplinary fields with diverse methods and theoretical commitments. Predictive coding neuroscience is a clear example: its literature spans computational theory, electrophysiology, imaging, behavior, and modeling, creating a synthesis problem that conventional meta-analysis cannot easily resolve.

item.title: Measurement-informed dynamical decoupling for fidelity preservation on large-scale quantum processors
item.description: Dynamical decoupling (DD) is a key technique for suppressing decoherence and preserving the performance of quantum algorithms. We introduce a measurement-based DD (MDD) protocol that determines control unitary gates from partial measurements of noisy subsystems, with measurement overhead scaling linearly with the number of subsystems.

item.title: Efficacy and safety of conscious/deep sedation versus general anesthesia in pulsed field ablation for atrial fibrillation: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: New work indexed under “Efficacy and safety of conscious/deep sedation versus general anesthesia in pulsed field ablation for atrial fibrillation: a systematic review and meta-analysis.” The source did not provide an abstract; read the original before evaluating its claims.

item.title: How many labels can a biological oscillator carry? A quality-factor screen for proposed information carriers
item.description: How many distinguishable labels can a biological oscillator carry? Proposals invoking collective vibrational modes, endogenous electromagnetic fields, microtubule excitations and oscillatory phase codes are each debated on grounds particular to themselves, with no shared standard for comparison.

item.title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information
item.description: Interpretability, AI auditing and assessments of machine consciousness increasingly rest on mechanism-level quantities: functionals of a system's causal transition law that describe how it computes, not what it outputs. Experiments see that law only through finite, partial and noisy interventions.

item.title: Invariance can prevent overfitting and shortcut learning in Quantum Neural Networks
item.description: Many image classification tasks have labels that are unchanged by rotations and reflections. Equivariant quantum neural networks incorporate such symmetries by design, but the specific benefit of symmetry is difficult to isolate.

item.title: PINNverse meets Jordan--Wigner: learning the Hamiltonian of long spin chains
item.description: Inverse physics-informed neural networks (PINNverse) learn the parameters of a quantum Hamiltonian from measured expectation values, but the network output grows as $4^N$ with the number of qubits $N$. We show that, for spin chains with nearest-neighbor exchange interactions, the Jordan-Wigner transformation removes this exponential cost: the dynamics closes on an $N\times N$ one-body density matrix, so the network needs only $N^2$ outputs and the data are local observables measured in five global settings.

item.title: Normalizing Flows for Classical Simulation of Quantum Circuits in Phase Space
item.description: We present a novel framework to learn a representation of quantum circuits based on the phase space formulation of many-body systems. Given that $N$-qubit states can be represented as probability distributions on a smooth $2N$-dimensional manifold, we show how unitary gates can be parameterized as normalizing flows between these distributions, opening a new avenue for quantum circuit simulation using generative models.

item.title: Assessing the expressive power of a gauge-invariant PEPS ansatz across a topological phase transition
item.description: We investigate the expressive power of the gauged Gaussian fermionic projected entangled pair state (GGFPEPS) ansatz, which is a manifestly gauge-invariant tensor network ansatz for $(2+1)$-dimensional lattice gauge theories. In the GGFPEPS ansatz, the gauge field on each link is represented by coupling its configuration to the fermion number of virtual fermions placed at both ends of the link.

item.title: Analog quantum approximate optimization algorithm for solving the weighted MaxCut problem on three-dimensional single-atom Rydberg array
item.description: We theoretically investigate an analog implementation of the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) for the weighted maximum cut problem (MaxCut) problem. The protocol uses a three-dimensional array of individually trapped Rydberg atoms driven by globally addressed laser pulses, with site-dependent detunings applied near the Rydberg resonance.

item.title: Fully GPU-accelerated semistochastic Epstein-Nesbet perturbation theory
item.description: Second-order Epstein-Nesbet perturbation theory (EN-PT2) is an important tool for improving selected configuration interaction (SCI) energies, but the large external determinant space creates substantial memory and communication costs on GPU clusters. We develop a fully GPU-accelerated implementation of distributed semistochastic EN-PT2, fusing excitation generation, screening, and PT2 weighting in a single kernel traversal.

item.title: Quantum algorithms
item.description: This chapter highlights quantum algorithms as a gate-based computational framework that exploits superposition, entanglement, and phase-coherent interference to realize demonstrable complexity reductions on selected problems. It begins by formally distinguishing quantum algorithms from classical deterministic and randomized computation through reversible unitary evolution, oracle-based problem access, and the measurement constraint that collapses quantum state information, thereby motivating amplitude-engineering…

item.title: Physical predictions in closed quantum gravity
item.description: A bstract Recent developments in gravitational path integrals indicate that the nonperturbative physical Hilbert space of a closed universe is one-dimensional within each superselection sector. This raises a basic puzzle: how can a unique quantum-gravity state give rise to semiclassical physics, measurement outcomes, and classical probabilities?

item.title: Quantum Machine Learning
item.description: Quantum machine learning (QML) has emerged as a rapidly developing field at the intersection of quantum computing, artificial intelligence, and data science. As quantum hardware and algorithms continue to advance, there is a growing need for a rigorous and accessible text that explains how quantum principles can be used to design, analyze, and implement machine learning models.

item.title: Decoding sequence auditory expectations for clinical diagnostic and prognostic assessment of prolonged disorders of consciousness
item.description: OBJECTIVE: Electroencephalogram (EEG) features are important objective markers for diagnostic and prognostic evaluation of prolonged disorders of consciousness (DOC). However, task-based EEG paradigms are limited by mismatches between task demands and patients' residual awareness, as well as the limited individual assessment capacity of machine-learning-based detection frameworks.

item.title: Dynamics of Rényi entanglement entropies and Eigenstate Thermalization
item.description: How is entanglement dynamics encoded in the eigenstates of the time-evolution operator? We address this question by focusing on Rényi entropy dynamics in deterministic chaotic Floquet models in arbitrary dimensions.
